pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart stands tall (height 0.869, just above the real range). The awning nearly reaches the top and the wheels reach the paving, so it reads at once at thumbnail size. B: the console is a wide, low slab (height 0.61) set square in the middle, with an empty floor band below and the lever as a thin spike. Its row of buttons reads as pattern before the object is named.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the console and turn it three-quarters so one corner comes toward the viewer. Let it fill the card from top to bottom, and make the lever and gauges large enough to read at small size.

pairs.difference: A: the pair of sneakers sits low and wide (height 0.487, below the real range), with the top third of the card empty, but it is a tight diagonal group that reads quickly. B: the helmet is one centered lump with a margin of 0.151, above the real range, and wide bands of empty pink wall and pale floor around it. It reads clearly but sits small and static, like a product shot.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the helmet so it almost touches the left and right edges, tilt it slightly, and cut the empty floor below it.

pairs.difference: A: the orange player sits upper left and the white cable and earbuds sweep down right, an off-center diagonal that fills the card, though the thin cable weakens at thumbnail size. B: the saucer is a flat horizontal band across the middle (height 0.467, below the real range), with its rim close to both side edges and equal empty yellow above and below. It is named instantly but leaves the card half empty.
pairs.fix: Tilt the saucer steeply toward the viewer so the dome and underside both show, and make it taller on the card so it fills the space above and below.

pairs.difference: A: the submarine is a big, heavy mass filling the middle, and the periscope and propeller break out toward the top and left. It is large against the dark green and reads first. B: the rocket is a clean diagonal in the center, but thin for the card (area 0.252, margin 0.11, near the top of the real range), with even blue space on all sides. Both read instantly, so the gap is small.
pairs.fix: Make the rocket larger and thicker in the body, with the nose and flame nearly reaching opposite corners of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the whole dome sits fully inside the card, shifted left, with a tunnel attached and a large crater at lower right. At thumbnail size the crater competes with the dome and the hero is small inside a full scene. B: the pool bar is cropped hard by the top and right edges, with the roof running off the card, close-in framing like the real van and fan cards. It is busy, but the drinks and fruit lead the eye.
pairs.fix: Move in close on the dome so it fills the card and is cropped slightly by one edge. Remove the big crater, or shrink it to a small dent behind the dome.

pairs.difference: A: the planet is a centered ball inside a thin ring, and the ring sets a wide, shallow box (width 0.907, height 0.531, width above and height below the real range). The ring tips nearly touch the sides, while the ball itself takes only about half the card, with stripes empty around it. B: the two sandals make a large tilted diagonal, top right to bottom left, with a compact, heavy read at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Make the planet ball much larger, filling most of the card height, with a thicker ring that runs off or nearly touches the card edges at a steeper angle.

pairs.difference: A: the rose arch stands whole and centered with a soft floor and matches the arch among the real cards. B: the column is cropped by the bottom edge (margin 0.0, area 0.484, above the real range) and pushed in close, with a gold sign at lower right that competes a little. Close cropping is common on real cards, and the sign is an unusual choice but not a tell. The composition gives no firm reason to choose.

A: the red scarf hangs centered and tall, with the gold badge as a clear focal point in the middle. It reads as one strong symmetrical shape. B: the meteor rock sits left of center with flames trailing to the upper right, a wide 0.853 by 0.604 box. The grey-brown rock is the largest mass but quiet, and the orange flames take the eye first, so the first read splits between tail and rock.
pairs.fix: Make the rock larger and more central, tilted along a steep diagonal, with the flames shorter and hugging the rock so the rock is seen first.

pairs.difference: A: the dish on its base is large and tilted and fills the card top to bottom (height 0.873), with the dish rim close to the top edge. It is a single clear read with open desert around it. B: the sand castle is a broad cluster of towers with a green bucket and blue shovel at lower right. The bright props pull attention from the sand-colored hero against the sand ground. Hierarchy alone favors A, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Crop in so the base is cut by the bottom edge and the dish reaches past one side edge, and leave out empty desert around it.

pairs.difference: A: the tiered fountain is centered and whole, wide at the base, cropped by nothing, with a tall stack that reads at once. B: the bumper car sits low with its pole cut by the top edge (margin 0.0), and the yellow floor stripe runs off the lower right. Both framings have equivalents on real cards: centered and whole like the barrel, and cropped by an edge like the fan. Neither gives a reason to choose.

A: the binoculars lie on a diagonal and are chunky and close, a dense mass (area 0.324) that reads at once, with both lenses facing the viewer. B: the telescope is a long thin diagonal on three thin legs (area 0.203, below the real range), with large gaps of stripe and grey ground around it. At thumbnail size only the tube reads, and the mount and legs thin out.
pairs.fix: Draw the telescope much thicker and closer, with the tube running off or nearly touching the upper right corner and the tripod short and sturdy, cropped by the bottom edge.

pairs.difference: A: the taxi fills the card width (0.926, just above the real range) in a three-quarter view, with its nose near the left edge and white road lines pointing into it. B: the rover is the smaller hero, sitting in the center with open grey ground and craters in front, and the dish and solar panel rise as thin add-ons. The body is only about half the card width and the lunar ground takes the bottom third.
pairs.fix: Bring the rover closer so its body fills the card width and its wheels reach the bottom edge. Enlarge the dish and cut the empty ground in front.

pattern: On composition, generated cards keep the whole object inside the frame. It sits in the middle at a safe size, with even space on all sides and a band of empty ground or wall, like a product shot. Real cards commit harder: they move closer, crop against an edge, or pack a heavy mass into the card. Thin or flat heroes (saucer, telescope, ring planet) are the clearest cases, because their bounding box looks fine while the mass inside it stays small. The signal is modest. Several pairs fall inside the real ranges on every measure, so confidence is low where the framing overlaps, and p07 and p10 give no reason to choose.
